name: Hattic
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct, attested only in Hittite-archive cuneiform; existing studies (e.g. Soysal 2004) do not establish word stress.

sources.citation: Simon, Zsolt 2012. Untersuchungen zur hattischen Grammatik: Phonologie, Morphologie und Syntax. PhD dissertation, Eotvos Lorand University, Budapest. 282 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 2.1.3.2.1 pp. 43-49: scriptio plena is meaningful; 'Was die Moeglichkeit des Akzents ausschliesst, ist die Beobachtung, dass es viele Faelle gibt, wo plene geschriebene Vokale zweimal innerhalb des gleichen Wortes vorkommen' (p. 48); concludes plene marks vowel length (p. 49). Research history pp. 24-28: Kassian 2010 was the first to address plene/accent at all. No stress position stated.

sources.citation: Kassian, A. S. 2010. Xattskij jazyk [Hattic]. In N. N. Kazansky, A. A. Kibrik, Yu. B. Koryakov (eds.), Jazyki mira: Drevnie reliktovye jazyki Perednej Azii, 168-184. Moskva: Academia.
sources.note: p. 173: the only possible indication of vowel prosody is plene spelling; its phonetic value in Hattic is not established; the Hittite reading (plene = old stressed syllable) is unsatisfactory for Hattic because plene occurs in several syllables of one phonetic word; perhaps vowel length, or a dictation artefact. No stress position stated.

sources.citation: Kammenhuber, Annelies 1969. Das Hattische. In J. Friedrich et al., Altkleinasiatische Sprachen (Handbuch der Orientalistik I.2.1-2.2), 428-546. Leiden: Brill.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number OL 330.5 Bd. 2, pt. 1/2, no. 2); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number OL 330.5 Bd. 2, pt. 1/2, no. 2
sources.note: p. 447 Anm. 2: plene vowel spellings not marked, Hattic vowel writing varies strongly; p. 488: 'Ob die gesprochene Sprache etwa Akzentunterschiede bei den verschiedenen Kasus in der Stammform kannte.. muss vorerst - vielleicht auch fuer immer - unbeantwortet bleiben.' No stress rule.

sources.citation: Koryakov, Yu. B. 2010. Drevnie reliktovye jazyki Perednej Azii (editors' introduction). In Jazyki mira: Drevnie reliktovye jazyki Perednej Azii, p. 15.
sources.note: Comparison of vocalism across Sumerian, Elamite, Hurrian, Urartian, Hattic limited to quality because cuneiform does not consistently record vowel length; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Schuster, Hans-Siegfried 1974. Die hattisch-hethitischen Bilinguen. I. Einleitung, Texte und Kommentar, Teil 1 (Documenta et Monumenta Orientis Antiqui 17). Leiden: Brill.
sources.note: scanned text (garbled) in the chapter on the Hattic material: whether Hattic verse was purely quantitative or an alternation of stressed and unstressed syllables can never be read off the script; one passing remark on vowel elision in an '(unbetonten offenen) Silbe -ni-'. No stress rule.
